# zone_mail_autoreply (Resource)

An automatic reply on a mailbox or a forwarder.

This is a separate resource rather than a block on `zone_mail_account` because the identical object hangs off both mailboxes **and** forwarders, from two endpoints. Folding it into the mailbox would leave forwarder autoreplies unmanageable. It also matches how people work: a vacation message is set and cleared on a different schedule from provisioning a mailbox.

~> **Destroying this disables the autoreply rather than leaving it in place.** The endpoint has no delete, but it can express "off", so that is what destroy does — unlike the other resources here whose objects the API cannot remove.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An autoreply on a mailbox. target says which endpoint to use, because the
# same object hangs off both mailboxes and forwarders.
resource "zone_mail_autoreply" "holidays" {
  service_name = "virt1.example.com"
  target       = "account"
  address      = zone_mail_account.info.address

  subject = "Out of office"
  body    = <<-EOT
    Thank you for your message. Our office is closed until 2 January.

    For anything urgent, please write to urgent@example.com.
  EOT

  date_start = "2026-12-24"
  date_end   = "2027-01-02"
}

# The same resource, on a forwarder rather than a mailbox.
resource "zone_mail_autoreply" "sales_closed" {
  service_name = "virt1.example.com"
  target       = "forwarder"
  address      = zone_mail_forwarder.sales.address

  body    = "Sales enquiries are handled from 2 January."
  enabled = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `address` (String) The mailbox or forwarder address this autoreply belongs to.
- `body` (String) The message body.
- `service_name` (String) The webhosting service this belongs to. This is a virtual server name, which often looks like a domain but is a different namespace from a DNS zone — use the `zone_vservers` data source to list the valid values. Changing it moves the resource to another service, which means replacing it.
- `target` (String) Whether `address` names a mailbox or a forwarder: `account` or `forwarder`. The two are separate endpoints serving the same object, so this has to be stated rather than guessed — guessing would mean a speculative extra request on every read, out of a budget of 60 a minute.

### Optional

- `date_end` (String) Last day to reply, as `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- `date_start` (String) First day to reply, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Leave both dates unset to reply until the autoreply is disabled.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the autoreply is sending. Set it to `false` to keep the text but stop replying.
- `from_name` (String) The name the reply appears to come from.
- `subject` (String) The reply's subject line.

### Read-Only

- `resource_url` (String) API URL of this autoreply.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Autoreplies are imported as "<service name>/<target>/<address>", where target
# is "account" or "forwarder".
terraform import zone_mail_autoreply.holidays "virt1.example.com/account/info@example.com"
```
